clue.text: Style shown by swimmer, footballer and oarsman

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football
the stroke is the rower who sets the pace in a crew

explanation.surface: A sporting style common to a swimmer, a footballer and a rower.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimmers use several recognised strokes, one of them swum lying face up.

clue.text: Composer means to live alone

explanation.definitionFit: J S Bach is the German Baroque composer; in New Zealand slang to bach is to keep house as a bachelor.

clue.text: Two names for beverage at classy foreign mansion

parts.note: cha and tea are two words for the same drink
cha and tea are two words for the same drink
U is the crossword abbreviation for upper-class

explanation.surface: Two words for a drink served at a smart foreign house.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA is a British slang word for tea. U stands for upper-class, as in 'U and non-U'.
explanation.definitionFit: A French country house or castle bears this name, so it is a grand residence abroad.

clue.text: Display of flamenco, say, may be mounted in Rome

explanation.surface: A flamenco show might be staged in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish Steps are the famous flight of stairs in Rome; flamenco is a Spanish dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Dance moves of Iberian origin, as in flamenco; Rome's famous stairway climbing from Piazza di Spagna.

clue.text: Issued shares as one gets on in trade, perhaps

indicators.note: in puts the one and on inside the rearranged trade
perhaps says trade is just one possible arrangement of these letters

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A company issued shares while someone gets ahead in business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TRADE into RATED; 'in' puts I and ON inside it. 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rationing gives out a limited portion to each person, so goods are allotted in fixed amounts.

clue.text: King leads a charge in unarmed fighting

indicators.note: leads puts the king first, before the rest

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A king leads a charge into a fight without weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese martial art uses hands and feet rather than weapons.

clue.text: Festive occasion knight had to leave

indicators.note: the word had is told to depart from the knight's name, so it is taken out

parts.note: Sir Galahad is the purest knight of the Round Table

explanation.surface: A knight had to quit a party early.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a grand celebration or festivity, such as a swimming gala.

clue.text: Ill-humour in an East Texan town

indicators.note: in sets the ill-humour inside the a-n plus East run

parts.note: bile is bad temper, from the old humour

explanation.surface: Bad temper in a town in eastern Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: Abilene is in west-central Texas, so 'East' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Abilene is a city in Texas, also famous as a Kansas cattle town.

clue.text: Fall caused by this projecting cartilage

explanation.surface: A fall caused by a lump of gristle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' is the Fall of Man in Genesis, when Adam ate the forbidden fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating the forbidden fruit brought about humanity's expulsion from Eden; the lump at the front of the throat is the larynx's protruding cartilage.

clue.text: Cards played at some stage

explanation.surface: Playing cards at some point in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards are eccentric or amusing people; parts acted in a theatre are the roles an actor takes on.

clue.text: Is required to enter state?

indicators.note: Is is told to go into the state abbreviation, so it sits inside it

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Asking what is needed to get into a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is the travel document a foreign country demands before admitting a visitor.

clue.text: Original status of New Year custom

parts.note: first means original or earliest
footing is standing or status, as in an equal footing

explanation.surface: The origins of a New Year tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland and northern England, the first person to cross the threshold after midnight on New Year's Eve brings luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogmanay tradition holds that the first visitor through the door brings luck for the year.

clue.text: Some criticise minister in the House

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: In Parliament, a few people attack a government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'in the House' as the definition, but that phrase cannot replace the answer; 'in the' is a link and 'House' alone defines it, despite looking like Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is the British short form for a semi-detached house, one joined to its neighbour by a shared wall.

clue.text: Aren't they in with a chance?

definitions.text: Aren't they in with a chance?

parts.words: Aren't they in with a chance?
parts.note: read literally, these are people who are not in, i.e. out; read normally, they are long shots given little hope of winning

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about contenders who might win.
explanation.definitionFit: Long shots in a race are rank no-hopers, and people not inside a group are excluded from it.

clue.text: Paying for public relations of one board

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Payment for the PR work of a company board.
explanation.definitionFit: A paying business makes money, earning more than it spends.

clue.text: Approximate shape and colour on bird, say

indicators.note: say means the two words are heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: a ruff is a wading bird and a hue is a colour; on puts the colour after the bird

explanation.surface: Describing the rough outline and plumage colour of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: RUFF and HUE spoken one after the other give the sound of the answer. 'on' in an across clue places the colour after the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To rough-hew is to shape timber or stone crudely, without finishing it.

clue.text: "Dear God! The very houses seem --' (Wordsworth)

parts.note: the missing word completes a line from the sonnet Composed upon Westminster Bridge, describing London still at dawn

explanation.surface: A quotation from Wordsworth with its final word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Wordsworth's sonnet 'Composed upon Westminster Bridge', about early-morning London; it ends 'And all that mighty heart is lying still!'
explanation.definitionFit: Houses at dawn seem to be sleeping, as the city has not yet woken.

clue.text: Pound a salesman wanted for shrub

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
a vender, or vendor, is a seller

explanation.surface: A salesman is wanted to sell a pound of shrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic purple-flowered bush is grown in gardens for its scent.

clue.text: Part 28. perhaps, needed to start bridge

definitions.text: Part 28. perhaps, needed to start bridge

parts.words: Part 28. perhaps, needed to start bridge
parts.note: a quarter is a part; the compass bearing at 28 is one of four bridge seats; a game of bridge cannot start without four players

explanation.surface: Asking which piece is needed before a bridge game can begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 across is EAST, one of the four seats at a bridge table; a bridge game needs four players, so the last arrival makes up the four.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter is one of four equal portions, and a player completing a four-handed table is the last of four.

clue.text: Downs so paradoxically described?

parts.note: chalk hills called downs are high ground, so a word meaning raised country seems the opposite of their name

explanation.surface: A question about the odd naming of rolling hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The Downs are ranges of chalk hills in southern England, such as the South Downs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilly or high country lies above the surrounding plain, which is what downs are.

clue.text: National emblem to remove, back in Irish house

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the name of the Irish house

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

indicators.note: back says the word for remove is read from right to left

parts.note: to doff is to remove, as with a hat

explanation.surface: Removing a national symbol and returning it to an Irish home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DOFF into FFOD, and 'in' puts it inside DAIL, the Irish parliament's lower house.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow spring flower is the national emblem of Wales.

clue.text: Seeing Land's End, many in crew show pleasure

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here taken from Land

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

indicators.note: in puts the many inside the crew

parts.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number

explanation.surface: A rowing crew is happy to see the tip of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the westernmost tip of Cornwall in England; here it means the last letter of LAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight is great joy or enjoyment.

clue.text: Like walrus after swallowing first of oysters

definitions.text: Like walrus after swallowing first of oysters

indicators.note: swallowing means the walrus takes the letter inside it

parts.note: morse is an old word for a walrus

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of oysters

explanation.surface: How the walrus feels after eating the oysters.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's poem 'The Walrus and the Carpenter', the Walrus weeps over the oysters he has eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and gloomy, as the tearful Walrus was in Carroll's poem.

clue.text: What sort of call is there for the peel on bananas?

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so these letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A joke question about what you call banana skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas', meaning mad, is the anagram signal: the letters of THE PEEL ON are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone call is a kind of call, made by ringing someone up.

clue.text: Paintwork Jack assumes to be dry

explanation.surface: A sailor puts on paint to keep the rain out.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack, or Jack Tar, is a traditional name for a sailor, who puts on oilskins in wet weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil paintings are a painter's works; oilskins are waterproof clothing a sailor puts on against rain and spray.

clue.text: Flower-girl's endless bad temper

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Irish is temper, as in getting one's Irish up

explanation.surface: A flower seller's constant bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower-girl' is a double-duty definition: the answer is both a flower and a girl's name. 'Getting your Irish up' means losing your temper.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded iris is a garden flower, and the name is also a woman's name.

clue.text: Knot or bow

explanation.definitionFit: A sheet bend is a sailor's knot; to bow is to stoop or curve forward.

clue.text: Avaricious female with prospects?

explanation.surface: A greedy woman who has good prospects.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman courting rich men for money is a mercenary type; a prospector digs for precious metal.

clue.text: Bearing of a Rugbeian

explanation.surface: The way a Rugby schoolboy carries himself.
explanation.walkthrough: A Rugbeian is a pupil of Rugby School; Harry East is Tom's friend there in the novel Tom Brown's School Days.
explanation.definitionFit: One compass point is a direction or bearing; the novel's Rugby pupil Harry has this surname.

clue.text: Sets aside broken Easter eggs

indicators.note: broken eggs are smashed apart, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Putting aside some smashed chocolate eggs at Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: To segregate is to separate or isolate one group from the rest.
